rationale: The mass reads as a split-bridge composition with one dominant horizontal connector and a notched void, so the primary gesture is understandable in all four views. Hierarchy is only moderate because several slabs and vertical cuts compete with the main bridge, creating some fragmentation. The silhouette avoids a pure stair-step logic, but the mass still depends on multiple offset plates and partial stepbacks. The central void is legible yet feels more like an interstitial notch than a robust public courtyard or undercut ground condition. Repair integrity is middling: the pieces look close to overlapping or clipped in a few views, though the overall assembly remains coherent. The precedent signal is decent, especially through bridge/split and undercut/courtyard ideas, but it does not strongly resolve into a single iconic precedent type.
warnings: Some volumes appear to collide or nearly overlap across views.
The form may be over-partitioned into too many thin surface pieces.
Void logic is present but not yet spatially generous.
